column3: NKJV renders the rare phrase בְּרִיר חַלָּמוּת (“juice of mallow/purslane”) as “the white of an egg.”
The line is difficult; NKJV renders “Though in anguish, I would exult, He will not spare,” taking the unsparing one as God.
Close to the Hebrew; וְתֻשִׁיָּה (“sound wisdom, resource”) is rendered “success.”
The Hebrew is terse; NKJV supplies “should be shown” and reads the second line as concessive, “Even though he forsakes.”
NKJV follows the written text (“not”), rendering “you are nothing,” where the read text gives “you have become [like] it.”
Close to the Hebrew; נִּמְרְצוּ (“they are painful”) is rendered “How forceful.”
Close to the Hebrew; “you would cast [lots] over the fatherless” is rendered “you overwhelm the fatherless,” and “bargain over” “undermine.”
Close to the Hebrew; הַוּוֹת (“calamities”) is rendered “the unsavory.”
